title.plain_text: Sample: Start mornings with 5 minute meditation

rich_text.plain_text: Mornings start with my phone and the day feels rushed before it begins.
Five quiet minutes first, so the day starts from my own pace instead of my inbox.
Leave the cushion out by the window. Set a five minute timer. Phone stays in the kitchen until after.
Strong start, most mornings for the first couple of months. Fell apart during the launch crunch and again during the move. Comes back each time, but never quite as steady as at the start.

title.plain_text: Sample: Put my phone away an hour before bed

rich_text.plain_text: I keep scrolling in bed and then lie awake wired.
Better sleep and a calmer head at night.
Charge the phone outside the bedroom. Keep a book on the nightstand.
Tried a few nights here and there. Haven't actually started properly.

title.plain_text: Sample: Say no to extra work I don't have room for

rich_text.plain_text: Every busy stretch starts with me saying yes to one more thing.
Protect time and energy for the work that matters and for rest.
Wait a day before agreeing to new requests. Write a short script for saying no kindly.
Said no once and felt good about it. Then said yes to three more things during the launch.
Realised it had been ages since I talked with my sister about anything real.
Stay close to the people who matter, not just when something needs organising.
Put a recurring reminder in the calendar. Keep calls short so they're easy to say yes to.
Still mostly logistics calls. The reminder keeps getting snoozed.
Whole days pass without going outside.
Fresh air and movement, and a break between work and evening.
A loop around the block after lunch.
Became automatic after a few weeks. Even kept it up through the busy stretches.
This one stuck because it was small and had a fixed place in the day.
Friends keep asking about the balcony plants.
Share what I'm learning and keep a record of it.
Pick a name. Write three short posts before publishing anything.
Wrote two drafts. Lost interest once work got busy.
Letting this go. I like the plants more than writing about them.
Wanted something slow and hands-on that isn't a screen.
A calming skill, and good bread.
Start with a simple no-knead loaf.
Flat loaves at first, then a good one. Now a regular thing.
Proud of this. Baking became a way to slow down.

title.plain_text: Sample: Ask for feedback on a bigger role

rich_text.plain_text: I keep doing lead work without the title or support.
Be clear about what I want at work and ask for it.
List what I already do. Book time with my manager.
Had the first conversation. Waiting on next steps.
Every time I open it something falls out.
A calmer home with less to manage.
One shelf at a time. Donate bag by the door.
Done before the move, which made packing much easier.
Small win that made a hard stretch lighter.
Headaches in the afternoon, usually on days I forget to drink anything.
Fewer headaches and more steady energy.
A full bottle on the desk every morning.
Mostly doing it. Forget on busy days.
Found an old sketchbook while unpacking.
Make something just for fun.
Ten minutes, any subject, no erasing.
A handful of sketches so far. Enjoying it.

Meet neighbours and get my hands in the dirt.
Sign up for the mailing list.
On the mailing list. Haven't gone yet.

title.plain_text: Sample: Plan a quiet day away

rich_text.plain_text: Need a day with no plans and no screens.
Real rest, somewhere that isn't home.
Pick a nearby town with a trail.
Just an idea for now.
